# MetaForge for opencode

**Generated by `scripts/build_integrations.py`. Do not edit by hand.**

The hosted MetaForge gateway as an MCP server in opencode, with the same commands, agents and skills as the Claude Code package and its working rules. The server is `metaforge`, at `https://mcp.staging.metaforge.uk/mcp`.

## Install

```
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/FidelOdok/MetaForge.git
sh MetaForge/integrations/opencode/install.sh --project /path/to/your/project
# or, for every project:
sh MetaForge/integrations/opencode/install.sh --global
```

`--project` installs into the project's `.opencode/` folder, `--global` into `~/.config/opencode/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode`). The script copies the commands, agents, skills and rules, then adds two entries to the `opencode.json` in that folder, creating it if there is none:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "metaforge": {
        "type": "remote",
        "url": "https://mcp.staging.metaforge.uk/mcp"
      }
    }
  },
  "instructions": [
    ".opencode/metaforge-rules.md"
  ]
}
```

Everything else in the file is kept, and the old file is saved as `opencode.json.bak`. A `metaforge` server you already have is left as it is. A file with comments (`opencode.jsonc`) is not rewritten; the script prints the entries for you to add. A global install writes the rules file's absolute path instead of the relative one. It needs `python3`.

By hand: copy `commands/`, `agents/`, `skills/` and `metaforge-rules.md` into `.opencode/`, and add the entries above. In a project with no `.opencode/opencode.json` yet, copying `opencode.json` there as well does the same.

## Sign in

```
opencode mcp auth metaforge
```

Sign in with your MetaForge email and password, the ones you use on the dashboard. There is no token or API key to enter: the gateway answers 401 and opencode runs OAuth, then keeps the credentials outside your config. You reach only your own account's projects. Inside opencode, `/mcps` does the same. `opencode mcp logout metaforge` signs out.

Do not add an `Authorization` header or set `oauth: false`. An API key skips the per-account scope the sign-in gives you.

## Writes wait for a human

A tool that writes is held for approval, because the hosted gateway sees opencode as a remote caller. Held calls appear on the dashboard's Approvals page, and `/metaforge/approvals` lists them.

## Commands

- `/metaforge/connect`
- `/metaforge/new`
- `/metaforge/use`
- `/metaforge/status`
- `/metaforge/design`
- `/metaforge/fea`
- `/metaforge/flow`
- `/metaforge/verify`
- `/metaforge/replan`
- `/metaforge/gate`
- `/metaforge/approvals`
- `/metaforge/imagine`
- `/metaforge/drive`
- `/metaforge/doctor`

When signed in, the gateway's own MCP prompts also appear, as `/metaforge:<name>`. They are the same workflows with wording for any client; the `/metaforge/<name>` commands are written for opencode and work before you sign in.

## Agents

Subagents (`mode: subagent`), launched by the main agent or by asking for one by name:

- `metaforge-flow-planner`
- `metaforge-gate-reviewer`
- `metaforge-run-verifier`

## Skills

52 skills, in `skills/metaforge/<id>/SKILL.md`. opencode reads `SKILL.md` skills natively, takes the id from the folder name, and lists each to the model by its description; the agent loads one with the `skill` tool, or you can with `@<id>`.

## Rules

`metaforge-rules.md` holds the working rules the Claude Code package adds at session start, loaded through `instructions`. It also says how opencode names the tools: `flow.propose` is `metaforge_flow_propose`.

Not carried over as a hook: Claude Code's reminder after a held `flow.propose` or `flow.patch`. It is a line in the rules instead. An opencode plugin could add it after the tool returns, but MCP tools run inside Code Mode by default, and whether the plugin hook sees that call could not be checked without signing in, so no plugin ships.

## What is verified

Loaded with opencode **2.2.5** in a scratch home directory, once installed with `--project` and once with `--global`:

- `opencode mcp list` prints `metaforge  needs authentication`: the server is configured, reached the hosted address and got its 401. On a freshly started opencode the first call can print `No MCP servers configured` before the connection starts; run it again.
- `opencode debug agents` lists the three agents with `mode: subagent`.
- The server's `GET /api/command` lists all 14 `/metaforge/<name>` commands and `GET /api/skill` all 52 skills (through `opencode api get`).
- The log shows `metaforge-rules.md` loaded from `instructions`, and no warning about any file in this package.

Not verified here: signing in and calling a tool, which needs a MetaForge account. The hosted gateway publishes OAuth metadata with dynamic client registration, which is the path opencode uses for a server that does not offer a client metadata document.

The formats come from that binary and the V2 documentation it links (https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/). If a later opencode stops loading them, re-check against your version first.
